text:
maria: Heads-up: saw a 12-18% p99 regression on a Mixtral 8k chat workload after yesterday's kernel-picker change. Dumping notes here.
alex: ack, can you paste the trace/where it's coming from?
maria: main hotspot looks like KV cache cold path + extra memcpy on handoff between micro-batches. stack traces point to kernel_select -> kv_prefetch -> memcpy
sasha: interesting — were these requests with long system prompts / chat templates? those push prefix lengths high and change kernel choice.
maria: yes, median prefix was ~900 tokens due to long chat template + few instructions. We fell back from the fused-rope kernel to the byte-friendly path.
jon: @maria can you share the perf-bot profile link? perf-bot: profiling job #1855004321 completed: https://perf.redwood/jobs/1855004321 — summary attached in logs
maria: pasted snippet:
```
hotspots:
- kv_prefetch (42% cpu)
- memcpy (18% cpu) — between worker A -> worker B
- kernel_dispatch (12% cpu) — fallback to byte-fallback kernel
```
alex: memcpy between A/B sounds like our KV handoff path. We added prefetching next micro-batch last week to reduce tail latency — maybe it's racing with blob copy.
sasha: also noticed RoPE scaling param for Mixtral was different in canary: scale=1.05 vs prod 0.98. RoPE scaling affects tokenization -> detokenization boundaries and can shift kernel heuristics.
jon: can that alter kernel selection heuristics? feels indirect.
alex: yes: kernel picker uses estimated seq_len distribution. If token counts change (due to byte-fallback causing different token boundaries for special tokens, BOS/EOS handling), prefix length estimate flips and we choose a different kernel.
maria: concrete repro: run chat template with long system prompt (6 lines) + user messages. On canary we see more byte-fallback tokens (special emoji + non-ascii) — that increased token count by ~7% and triggered fallback.
sasha: so root cause is interplay of tokenizer byte-fallback + RoPE tweak + our new prefetch copy. All combined.
jon: plan? revert kernel-picker change or make picker robust to small token-count variance.
alex: suggestion: change kernel-picker threshold margin from 10% to 20% for a 48h canary, and gate prefetch memcpy to be async/non-blocking (avoid A->B sync copy). Also add a quick KV handoff benchmark in CI.
maria: I'll open a PR with three changes: 1) bump picker margin, 2) make KV prefetch non-blocking, 3) add a regression unit test with long chat template + emoji. Draft link: https://git.redwood/prefs/kv-handoff-1855
sasha: add a test for RoPE scale combos + Mixtral/Llama/Qwen — we saw Llama unaffected but Qwen had similar token variance on non-ascii.
jon: for observability: add a per-request annotation for kernel variant + token_count_delta (tokenized_count - raw_estimate). That way we can see when tokenizer changes flip the kernel.
perf-bot: canary job queued for kv-handoff non-blocking change.
alex: small note: when making prefetch async, ensure we still populate KV cache before first token gen for low-latency requests. Use optimistic prefetch + fallback warmup.
maria: agreed. I'll run local microbench with sequence length distro: [100, 400, 900, 1200] and special token mix: emoji+non-ascii ~15%.
sasha: FYI: in Mixtral the head_dim is 128 vs Qwen 96. If we change head/kv dims aggressively, kernel-maker may pick different matmul kernels — include head_dim in logs.
jon: good call. let's capture model metadata (heads, kv_dim) in profiler output.
maria: timeline: PR by EOD, canary for 48h, revert if p99 > baseline+5%. I'll run a quick smoke now and post results.
alex: thanks — small follow-up: add short note in runbook about tokenizer-induced kernel flips; this has bit us twice.
maria: posted smoke run: p50 same, p95 +6%, p99 +2% (improved vs previous canary). attaching flame: https://perf.redwood/jobs/1855004321/flame
sasha: looks promising. If non-blocking prefetch works, we avoid the blocking memcpy jitter.
jon: awesome. once canary OK, ship to prod and then follow-up with longer-term: smarter kernel-picker that factors in observed tokenization delta and model head_dim.
maria: +1. closing loop after canary finishes. :thumbsup:
